_note: Every dependency below carries an evidence_url pointing at a document that explicitly names its source. The LGFF Capital Funding Allocation Formula fact sheet is unusually good evidence: it lists its input data sources by name, with links.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Capital Funding Allocations
reports.description: Annual allocation of provincial capital funding to Alberta local governments, calculated by a formula set out in the Local Government Fiscal Framework Act. $800 million in 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Aggregate amounts must be communicated by September 30 two years in advance; individual allocations follow some weeks later.

entries.covers: Future LGFF capital funding levels for the 2028 funding year

release_schedule.rule: The LGFF Act requires that information on future funding levels is shared by September 30, 2 years prior to the funding year.
release_schedule.note: Page (updated/published March 23, 2026) states the statutory disclosure deadline; the most recent occurrence (Sept 30, 2025, covering the 2027 funding year) has already passed, so the next occurrence is Sept 30, 2026. No published multi-year release calendar was found beyond this stated statutory rule.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Operating Funding
reports.description: Annual operating funding component of the Local Government Fiscal Framework, $60 million per year, distributed to Alberta local governments.

entries.covers: 2027 LGFF Operating funding payment to municipalities

release_schedule.rule: Funding is allocated annually after legislative approval of the program budget, and authorization of program funding and individual allocations by the Minister of Municipal Affairs. Payments to municipalities occur by approximately June 30, following provincial budget approval (conditional on certification of the prior year's Statement of Funding and Expenditures, matching reported expenditures to the allocation, and submission of the executed Memorandum of Agreement).
release_schedule.note: Date is described by the publisher's own guidelines as 'approximately June 30' — an annual target, not a guaranteed fixed date. The June 30, 2026 payment for the current cycle has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is projected for June 30, 2027. Sourced from the LGFF Operating Program Guidelines PDF (dated 2023-12-12, last modified 2024-03-12), linked from the publisher's 'Local Government Fiscal Framework program guidelines' Open Government page. Underlying allocation formula/amounts themselves are set via the provincial budget process (irregular relative to any fixed calendar date) but the annual payment-to-municipalities deadline is the stated recurring rule.

reports.title: Municipal Affairs Population List (MAPL)
reports.description: Annual official population counts for Alberta municipalities, Metis Settlements and First Nations communities, drawn from municipal or federal census results. Used by provincial ministries to determine municipal grants.
reports.cadence_note: Discontinued in 2020 with the repeal of the Determination of Population Regulation; resumed in 2023 under the Municipal Census Regulation.

release_schedule.note: The CKAN metadata for this dataset states 'updatefrequency: Annual' and shows resource creation dates for the last three editions: the 2023 population list was posted 2024-02-16, the 2024 population list was posted 2025-04-11, and the 2025 population list (most recent, current as of this query) was posted 2026-01-21. The list was discontinued after 2019 and publication resumed with the 2023 edition. Each numbered edition (e.g. '2025 population list') is published roughly a year after its reference year, but the exact month varies (Jan/Feb/Apr), so no single stated day exists. Next expected release would be the '2026 population list', likely appearing sometime between roughly January and June 2027 based on this pattern.

reports.title: Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates
reports.publisher: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, Office of Statistics and Information
reports.description: Annual population estimates for Alberta census subdivisions by year, age and gender, including permanent and non-permanent residents.

entries.covers: Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates, next annual update (2016-2026)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar found on Alberta.ca or the open.alberta.ca/open.canada.ca dataset pages. The dataset's own resource-update history shows the CSD-level municipal population estimates file has been refreshed in mid-January in the years for which we have confirmed dates: updated January 11, 2023 (covering 2016-2022) and updated January 14, 2026 (covering 2016-2025), consistent with a once-a-year January update pattern (releases_per_year=1 on file is consistent with this). No intervening years' exact update dates could be confirmed via search, so the pattern is based on two confirmed data points plus the current 'most recent update' timestamp; the office could be contacted directly (780-427-2071) to confirm exact cadence. The open.canada.ca dataset record lists overall dataset maintenance frequency as 'Quarterly', but that reflects the combined dataset (which also bundles a separate quarterly provincial-level population series updated June 17, 2026) rather than this specific municipal/CSD-level component, which itself only shows January updates.

reports.title: Municipal Financial Information Return (FIR)
reports.description: Standardised annual return summarising each municipality's audited financial statements — assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, long term debt and property taxes. Required from every Alberta municipality by May 1.
reports.cadence_note: Due May 1 for the preceding financial year.

release_schedule.rule: Each municipality and each regional services commission must prepare annual audited financial statements and a financial information return (FIR). Both reports must be returned to Alberta Municipal Affairs by May 1 of each year, as required by the Municipal Government Act.
release_schedule.note: The 2026-05-01 deadline (for the 2025 fiscal year FIR) has already passed relative to today's date (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is 2027-05-01. Extensions to this deadline can be requested and are evaluated by Municipal Affairs (see ma-financial-reporting-extension-requests.pdf), so an individual municipality's actual submission date could shift, but the standard statutory deadline is May 1.

reports.title: Municipal Financial and Statistical Data
reports.description: Annual compilation of every Alberta municipality's financial and statistical returns, including tangible capital assets, accumulated amortization, road length, assessment and tax rates.

entries.covers: Statutory deadline for municipalities to submit FY2026 audited financial statements, FIR and SIR to Alberta Municipal Affairs, which Municipal Affairs then compiles into the next edition of this report

release_schedule.rule: A municipality is required to submit to Alberta Municipal Affairs, by May 1 of each year, its financial statements and auditor's report pertaining to the previous year, as well as a financial information return (FIR) that is a summary of information from the audited financial statements. Municipalities also submit statistical information returns (SIR) each year as required under the Municipal Government Act.
release_schedule.note: This is the statutory submission deadline that feeds the compiled dataset, not a publication date Municipal Affairs itself commits to. CKAN metadata (open.alberta.ca API, checked 2026-08-11) confirms updatefrequency='Annual' and shows the 2025 financial-year resource already has real content as of last_modified 2026-08-05 (following the May 1, 2026 deadline for FY2025 data). Historically the compiled dataset resource for a given fiscal year has appeared/been substantively updated anywhere from ~1 to ~6+ months after the following May 1 deadline (e.g. FY2022 resource created 2023-06-05, FY2023 resource created 2024-08-29, FY2024 last substantively updated 2026-07-16), so the exact month the FY2026 edition appears cannot be pinned down beyond 'sometime after 2027-05-01'.

reports.title: Provincial Equalized Assessment Report
reports.description: Annual adjustment of every municipality's taxable assessment to a common basis, producing a uniform provincial measure of property wealth. Determines each municipality's share of requisitions.

release_schedule.note: Alberta Municipal Affairs publishes this annual series ('Provincial equalized assessment report', ISSN 2368-657X) on the Open Government portal every year, consistently in late October/early November. CKAN resource-creation timestamps for the last several editions: Provincial 2022 report created 2021-10-29; Provincial 2023 report created 2022-10-31; Provincial 2024 report created 2023-10-31; Provincial 2025 report created 2024-11-01; Provincial 2026 report created 2025-10-30 (this is the current/most-recent edition as of 2026-08-11). No formal forward-looking release calendar or stated statutory publication date was found — the pattern is inferred purely from past posting dates. The dataset's own metadata field 'updatefrequency' is listed as 'Annual'. Based on this pattern, the next edition (Provincial 2027 equalized assessment report) is expected in late October/early November 2026. NOTE: the corpus's existing url (open.alberta.ca/opendata/equalized-assessment-report) actually resolves to a different, related dataset titled 'Updated Equalized Assessment' (a supplemental mid-cycle update resource), not this annual 'Provincial equalized assessment report' series — see url_correction.

entries.covers: Provincial 2026 equalized assessment report (current/most recent edition)
Provincial 2027 equalized assessment report (next expected edition)

reports.title: Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report
reports.description: Annual statement of the education property tax requisition levied on each Alberta municipality, split between residential/farm and non-residential. Municipalities are obliged to collect it on the province's behalf. $3.1 billion in 2025.

release_schedule.note: Late-February window, 5 years running. Candidate edge, not yet added: this report methodologically depends on Alberta's 'equalized assessment' dataset, a separate Municipal Affairs publication — needs a proper basis before becoming a real edge.

dependencies.basis: Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight population at 48 per cent, and the fact sheet names Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates as the data source.
Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight education property tax requisitions at 48 per cent, sourced from the Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report.
Allocations to local governments other than Calgary and Edmonton weight population at 65 per cent, taken from the Municipal Affairs Population List.

Tangible capital assets (15 per cent), five-year average cumulative amortization (10 per cent) and length of local roads (10 per cent) are all drawn from named schedules of the Municipal Financial and Statistical Data.
Needs-based funding eligibility is set by comparing a municipality's equalized assessment per capita, or per kilometre of road, against the provincial average.
The dataset is compiled from the financial information return and statistical information return submitted annually by every Alberta municipality.

Alberta's education property tax page states the mechanism directly: 'Municipal Affairs establishes the provincial mill rate used to determine each municipality's share of the provincial education tax. The provincial equalized assessment base used to determine education property taxes this year reflects 2024 property values.' It gives the rates in force: 'Education property tax rates will increase to $2.84 per $1,000 of equalized assessment for residential/farmland properties and $4.17 per $1,000 of equalized assessment for non-residential properties in 2026-27', raising the requisition 'from $3.1 billion in 2025-26 to $3.6 billion in 2026-27'. Both figures verified verbatim. [Basis moved here 2026-08-07 from ontario-ompf-mpac.json, where it lived as a deliberately-superseding duplicate copy; see that file's _dropped note.]

reference_period.stated_as: Annual, with a two-year lag stated outright: 'The provincial equalized assessment base used to determine education property taxes this year reflects 2024 property values.' The reading is once a year against a base two years stale, which is a documented lag rather than an inferred one.
